Scenario Simulator

Test operational ideas without changing the source data. The simulator uses the historical behavior already loaded in this report and clearly separates observed results from estimated scenario results.

Scenario only · Actuals stay unchanged

1 · What if an operational KPI changes?

Select a client, optionally narrow to a country, choose a KPI and enter the final scenario value. The model translates the KPI movement into FTE/hour capacity where possible, recalculates PPH and BH, and then recomputes B2P. Historical data calibrates sensitivity; it does not decide whether a deterioration is "good" or "bad".

How to Read the Report

The report is built for operating decisions, not just reporting. Start with the portfolio result, identify the accounts creating the gap, understand whether the movement is structural or unusual, test a scenario, and then validate the source before acting. Every portfolio percentage uses the operating denominator that best represents that KPI; small accounts therefore do not carry the same weight as large accounts.

1Read the portfolioHealth, B2P, ABS, Attrition, Occupancy and staffing tell you whether the current scope is on track.
2Find the material gapUse attainment, Pareto and HotList to focus on the accounts that matter most.
3Diagnose the movementUse trends, momentum and correlation as diagnostic evidence — not as proof of causation.
4Test a decisionScenario Simulator translates KPI or FTE changes into an estimated operational effect.
5Validate the dataPossible Data Errors and Source Quality checks help separate a real signal from a loading issue.

Calculation Model

Target comparisons are calculated only on matched Actual + Target rows. The coverage percentage tells you how much of the operating base is represented by that comparison.

KPIPortfolio calculationInterpretation
Productive FTEActual = Σ FTE. Target gap = Σ Actual and Σ Target only on matched rows.Staffing is considered broadly aligned when Actual is within ±5% of Target.
PPHΣ PPHOperating-volume base used to weight B2P, MLOT and account-level portfolio Health.
B2PΣ(B2P × PPH) ÷ ΣPPHHigher is better. The displayed Actual vs Target comparison uses only rows where both values are available.
OccupancyΣ(Occupancy × Schedule Hours) ÷ ΣSchedule HoursHigher is treated as favorable. Values outside the valid 0–100% range are retained for QA but excluded from the weighted comparison.
AttritionΣ(Attrition × Productive FTE) ÷ ΣFTELower is better. Larger operations contribute proportionally more.
Total ABSΣ(Planned ABS Hours + Unplanned ABS Hours) ÷ ΣSchedule HoursLower is better. This is calculated from hours rather than averaging source percentages.
MLOTΣ(MLOT × PPH) ÷ ΣPPHLower is treated as favorable. Literal zeroes are preserved as real zeroes.
SRSΣ(SRS × Productive FTE) ÷ ΣFTEHigher is treated as favorable when a comparable target exists.
Main KPIDirection-adjusted Actual ÷ Target, weighted by PPH (FTE fallback only when PPH is unavailable).Only source KPI names whose direction can be mapped confidently are included.

Health, Priority & Coverage

These indicators answer different questions and should not be read as interchangeable.

Portfolio Health
Each account receives a pass/fail result for every valid KPI with a comparable target. Account Health is the share passed. Portfolio Health then weights the account by PPH; if an account has no PPH, Productive FTE is used as the fallback weight. Coverage uses the same weighting basis in numerator and denominator.
Priority Index
Combines unfavorable KPI severity with PPH. It is designed to rank operational review priority — it is not a financial loss estimate.
Target Coverage
The share of the relevant denominator that has both Actual and Target. A 55% FTE coverage means the target gap represents 55% of FTE, not the full portfolio.
Attainment
A common target scale where 100% means target met. Direction is adjusted first: for lower-is-better KPIs such as ABS and Attrition, a lower Actual produces higher attainment.
Adverse Gap
Only the unfavorable part of Actual versus Target. A KPI already better than target contributes zero adverse gap.
Pareto
Ranks the selected adverse impact and identifies the accounts that make up roughly the first 80% of it, helping focus attention on the few material drivers.

Source Quality Checks

12.44K source rows across 31 monthly periods and 14 countries. Raw source values are preserved; only values that fail a defined validation rule are excluded from the affected calculation.

Country name standardization
2 row(s) required normalization of capitalization/spacing (for example EL SALVADOR). No operating value was changed.
Applied
Repeated account-month rows
24 repeated Country + Client + Month rows were found. They are grouped through the KPI’s native weighting rather than dropped.

245 row(s) have blank/unknown Client Active status and remain available under Status = Unknown.
245

3 row(s) are above 100% Attrition. They remain source values and are visible for review.
3
Occupancy outside 0–100%
0 Actual and 3 Target row(s) fall outside the valid percentage range. Raw values are preserved for QA; invalid values are excluded only from Occupancy calculations.
0 A / 3 T
Literal MLOT zeroes
8428 MLOT row(s) contain a literal 0. They are preserved as zero and are not converted to missing values.

Data Rules & Guardrails

The report protects the analysis without silently rewriting the source.

Zero is not blankLiteral zeroes are preserved. A KPI with value 0 participates in the calculation when 0 is a valid source value.
Invalid % values are not averagedFor Occupancy, source values outside 0–100% are retained as raw QA values but excluded from the affected weighted KPI/target comparison.
No automatic data repairPossible Data Errors flags suspicious points for review; it never overwrites the source Actual or Target.
Coverage is explicitA target result is never presented as full-portfolio performance when only part of the denominator has a target.

KPI Glossary

Plain-language definitions of the source metrics and the weighting used in this report.

Productive FTE
Productive staffing reported for the account. Snapshot views sum FTE; when multiple months are intentionally selected, the report uses the average monthly FTE for the headline.
PPH
Paid/production-hour operating base supplied by the source. It is the native weighting denominator for B2P and MLOT and the preferred account weight for Portfolio Health.
BH
Billable Hours reconstructed in the simulator from the identity BH = B2P × PPH. BH is not independently loaded in this source file.
B2P
Billable-to-paid productivity ratio from the source. Portfolio B2P is weighted by PPH, not averaged equally by account.
Occupancy
Share of scheduled time represented by productive workload according to the source definition. Portfolio Occupancy is weighted by Schedule Hours.
Attrition
Source attrition rate. Portfolio Attrition is weighted by Productive FTE. Lower is treated as better.
Planned ABS
Planned absence hours divided by Schedule Hours.
Unplanned ABS
Unplanned absence hours divided by Schedule Hours.
Total ABS
Planned plus unplanned absence hours divided by Schedule Hours. The report calculates it from the hours themselves.
MLOT
MLOT percentage supplied by the source, weighted by PPH. Lower is treated as favorable for target comparison.
SRS
SRS score supplied by the source. Portfolio SRS is weighted by Productive FTE.
Main KPI
The account’s main operational KPI. The model maps KPI names to higher-is-better, lower-is-better or staffing-band logic before comparing Actual versus Target.

Analytics & Interaction Glossary

Definitions for the diagnostic views, visual interactions and anomaly logic.

Connected Filters
Period, Region (SubRegion), Country, Client, Industry and Status are searchable, multi-select filters. Each list only offers values still available in the current context.
Visual Cross-Filter
Clicking a selectable bar, bubble or account temporarily filters the other visuals, similar to Power BI. The top slicers remain unchanged and the visual selection can be cleared independently.
Correlation (r)
Measures how two KPIs move together linearly. +1 means they move together, -1 means they move in opposite directions, and values near 0 show little linear relationship. Correlation does not prove causation.
R²
Shows how tightly the observations fit the straight regression line. It describes linear fit, not operational causality.
Bubble Size
In correlation views, bubble size represents PPH so higher-volume account-country observations are visually more material.
Momentum
Current account Health minus the average Health of the prior three valid months. Positive values indicate recovery; negative values indicate deterioration.
Volatility
Robust measure of how unstable a KPI has been relative to its own recent history. It uses median-based dispersion so one extreme month does not dominate the measure.
Possible Data Error
A review flag for a point that is unusually far from the same account’s historical baseline. At least eight prior valid months are required before the model flags a statistical break.
Historical Baseline
Median of up to the prior 12 valid months for the same account and KPI. The median is more resistant to one-off outliers than a simple average.
Anomaly Score
Combines robust distance from baseline, relative size of the break and whether the surrounding months return toward normal. Higher means more unusual.
Region
Uses the source field SubRegion (Brazil, CAN, CSC, MAR, MEX, NCA or South Cone in the current file).
Matched Scope
Subset where Actual, Target and the KPI’s required weighting denominator are all available. This is the only scope used for a target comparison.

Scenario Simulator Method

The simulator separates operational math from historical association. It never changes the underlying source data.

KPI → B2P Scenario
For Attrition and ABS/SHKG drivers, the KPI movement is first translated into FTE/hour capacity. PPH and BH are then changed using trailing six-month productivity ratios and B2P is recomputed as BH ÷ PPH.
FTE-Equivalent Impact
Capacity translation, not a roster commitment. Attrition uses the rate change × current FTE. ABS/SHKG uses the rate change × Schedule Hours and converts those hours through recent Schedule Hours per FTE.
PPH/FTE & BH/FTE
Trailing six-month weighted operating productivity used for Attrition scenarios. These ratios convert the FTE-equivalent movement into changes in paid/production hours and billable hours.
PPH/Schedule & BH/Schedule
Trailing six-month hour productivity used for ABS/SHKG scenarios to translate changed capacity hours into PPH and BH.
Direction Guardrail
A deterioration in a lower-is-better driver such as Attrition or ABS is not allowed to appear as a B2P improvement solely because of a historical correlation or an unusual historical mix.
Historical Sensitivity
Weighted historical relationship between the selected KPI and B2P. For capacity drivers it is secondary: it is used only as a conservative guardrail/calibration if the raw operational bridge produces a direction that conflicts with the KPI logic.
Client-Only Scenario
Country can remain at All countries. The selected client is then consolidated across the countries still available under the global filters using each KPI’s native denominator.
FTE Reallocation Scenario
Moves FTE between two countries of the same client while keeping each country’s current B2P and PPH/FTE profile. It estimates mix/productivity effect only; it does not include cost, ramp, language or service-risk assumptions.
Scenario Confidence
Indicates how much comparable history exists and how stable the historical relationship has been. It is a confidence in the sensitivity evidence, not proof of cause.
